item.title: Managing Workspaces
item.description:
This guide walks you through the practical steps of managing your Workspaces. Here, you’ll learn how to create, edit, and delete Workspaces, as well as how to manage access by assigning teams and resources like Environments, Designs, and Views to them.

If you’re new to the concept of Workspaces, we recommend starting with the Workspaces Overview to understand what a Workspace is and how it relates to key components like Environments, Designs, and Teams.

item.title: Workspaces
item.description:
Workspaces and environments are how an organization decides which teams can read which connections and where its designs live. For the model, read Workspaces and Environments. For limits, defaults, and error messages, see Spaces.

item.title: Managing Environments
item.description:
This guide walks you through the practical steps of managing your Environments. Here you will learn how to see the Environments in your organization, create and edit them, review the Connections that belong to an Environment, and assign or remove those Connections.

If you are new to the concept of Environments, start with the Environments Overview to understand what an Environment is and how it relates to Connections, Credentials, and Workspaces.

item.title: Managing Profiles
item.description:
This guide shows how to manage profiles through the Layer5 Cloud API. Profiles have no page in the Layer5 Cloud UI yet. For the base URL and authentication, see the Cloud API. All paths below sit under /api.

A Note on Permissions

Each action needs the permission named beside it. A profile you cannot see, one that was deleted, and one that belongs to another organization all answer the same 404. See Default Permissions.

List profiles 🔗

GET /profiles (View Profiles) lists the profiles you can see in your current organization. Without View Profiles, it lists only the profiles you own. Pass orgId to choose another organization you belong to, userId to find the profile that represents a user, and search, order (name, createdAt or updatedAt), page and pagesize to page through the results.

item.title: Spaces
item.description:
Spaces is where an organization keeps its workspaces, environments, and the connections those environments hold. A workspace groups teams, environments, designs, and views. An environment groups connections into a deploy target. For the model, read Workspaces and Environments. For the tasks, use the workspace guides. For every endpoint’s schema, see the REST API Reference, and for base URL and authentication see the Cloud API. All paths below sit under /api.

Workspace and environment reference 🔗

Fields, defaults, and limits 🔗

Property Workspace Environment
Name Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API. Up to 255 characters. Not required or unique on the API.
Description Up to 255 characters. May be empty. Up to 255 characters. May be empty.
Organization Required on create. Fixed for the life of the workspace. Required on create (organizationId is required). Fixed for the life of the environment.
Owner The user who created it. Not recorded on create.
Starting state No teams, environments, designs, or views. No connections, in no workspace.
Kind Single kind. Ordinary when created through the API. Platform-provisioned environments exist and are protected.
Update Only the fields sent change. Name and description are both replaced; an omitted field becomes empty.
Plan check None. None. The feature matrix lists environments under Enterprise.
Count limits None. An organization must keep at least one workspace. None.

Layer5 Cloud creates My Workspace in any organization that has no workspace.

item.title: Workspaces
item.description:
A workspace is a named grouping inside an organization. It brings together the teams who do a piece of work, the environments they deploy to, and the designs and views they work on. A workspace does two separate jobs:

  • It organizes resources. Designs and views live in a workspace, and the workspace decides which organization they are listed under.
  • It grants connection access. Assigning a team to a workspace gives that team’s members read-only access to the connections in the workspace’s environments. That is the only access a team assignment grants.

You can create Workspaces to group related Designs and Environments and to decide which teams can read which connections.

item.title: Environments
item.description:
An environment is a named group of connections, such as Kubernetes clusters, together with the credentials those connections use. Environments matter for two reasons:

  • An environment is a deploy target. When you deploy a design, you choose the environment to deploy it to, and the design deploys to that environment’s connections.
  • An environment is how a workspace exposes connections. A workspace never holds connections directly. It holds environments, and teams assigned to the workspace reach the connections inside them.

Group connections the way you deploy: one environment per pipeline stage, region, or purpose. An environment belongs to one organization for its whole life. Editing an environment never changes its organization. Every member of the organization can list and open every environment in it. Team membership does not narrow the list.

item.title: Profiles
item.description:
A profile is a named record that belongs to one organization. It represents a person or a persona, such as the platform accounts someone publishes through, and it groups existing connections under that identity. Profiles are shared with people by assigning them to workspaces.

A profile is not your user account profile, and it is not a Meshery performance profile.

What a profile holds 🔗

  • a name (required, up to 255 characters, not unique) and an optional description (up to 1000 characters)
  • an owner, who must be a signed-in member of the profile’s organization
  • optionally, the user the profile represents
  • free-form metadata
  • links to connections. A profile links to connections that already exist; it never copies them. Removing a link leaves the connection untouched.

A profile can be assigned to any number of workspaces in its own organization. Its organization is fixed for the life of the profile.
